problem: Conventional discriminative reranking for parsing needs gold-standard reference parse trees, which are not naturally available in grounded language learning (following navigation instructions learned from observation).
motivation: Grounded language acquisition learns from ambiguous observation of instructions and their execution, with no annotated parses. Reranking could improve the base semantic parser, but only if it can be trained without gold trees. The observation is that response feedback (e.g. successful task completion) can serve as weak supervision instead.
key_idea: Adapt discriminative reranking to grounded navigation-instruction learning by training the reranker with weak response feedback (task completion success) in place of gold-standard parse trees.
insight: Only the abstract was available. It states that reranking trained on response feedback performs comparably to reranking trained on gold-standard parse trees, suggesting that execution success is a sufficient training signal for the reranker. No ablation details are available.
method: Base grounded semantic parser: produces n-best candidate parses of navigation instructions, learned from observation (details not available; abstract only).
Discriminative reranker: reranks the candidate parses to improve the top-ranked one.
Response-feedback supervision: labels or scores candidate parses by whether executing them completes the navigation task, replacing gold reference trees.

setting.backbone: Semantic parser with discriminative reranker (details not given in abstract)
setting.training_data: Navigation instructions paired with observed execution; response feedback from task completion (details not in abstract)

results: The abstract reports that reranking trained with response feedback performs comparably to reranking trained on gold-standard parse trees. No numbers are given in the abstract.
